title: Smooth pullbacks of coordinate-subspace blowups and their boundary charts
statement:
Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq0$, let $V$ be an $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $c:V\to\mathbf A^n_F$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ for the pulled-back coordinate functions. For any $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the scheme-theoretic coordinate intersection $C_A=V(z_a:a\in A)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] is smooth over $F$, is reduced and regular, and, when nonempty, has pure codimension $|A|$ in $V$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme]. At every point of $V$, the vanishing members of the coordinate list are distinct members of some regular system of parameters of its local ring [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. An empty $A$ gives $C_A=V$.

Fix nonempty $S\subseteq T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and put $B_T=V(\prod_{a\in T}z_a)$ and $D_S=V(\prod_{a\in S}z_a)$, as reduced effective Cartier divisors [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Let $b:V^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{C_S}V\to V$ be the ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. It is canonically the pullback along $c$ of the blowup of $\mathbf A^n_F$ in the coordinate subspace with indices $S$. It has an open cover $(V_j^+)_{j\in S}$ with smooth maps to affine $n$-space having coordinates $z_j$, $u_a=z_a/z_j$ for $a\in S\setminus\{j\}$, and $z_a$ for $a\notin S$. On $V_j^+$ the exceptional divisor has equation $z_j=0$, the reduced full inverse image of $B_T$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] has equation
$$z_j\prod_{a\in S\setminus\{j\}}u_a\prod_{a\in T\setminus S}z_a=0,$$
and the strict transform of $D_S$ [def-nagata-strict-transform] has equation $\prod_{a\in S\setminus\{j\}}u_a=0$. The corresponding coordinate intersections on these charts are smooth over $F$ of pure codimension equal to the number of chosen coordinate factors, and the vanishing chart coordinates extend to a regular system of parameters at every point. Empty charts and empty intersections are allowed; if $|S|=1$, the blowup is the identity and the strict transform of $D_S$ is empty. No perfection, integrality, separatedness or global quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First establish the assertions about a smooth coordinate map, for later use on both $V$ and its blowup charts. The scheme $C_A$ is the base change of $c$ to the coordinate affine space $\mathbf A_F^{n-|A|}$. Its projection to that space is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). That affine space is smooth over $F$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], so composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition] makes $C_A/F$ smooth. This includes $A=\varnothing$, and hence proves that $V/F$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] to each: they are locally Noetherian with regular local rings. Those local rings are domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], hence have no nonzero nilpotents, so these schemes are reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. No finite-type bound on all of $V$ or perfection of $F$ was used.

Fix $x\in V$ and let $L$ be any ordered subset of the coordinate indices vanishing at $x$. Put $P=F[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$, $y=c(x)$, $Q=P_{\mathfrak p_y}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{V,x}$. Smoothness makes $c$ flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; [def-weil-flat-morphism] says precisely that $Q\to R$ is flat. In $P$, after quotienting by any prefix of the distinct variables in $L$, multiplication by the next variable is injective: the quotient is the polynomial ring on the remaining variables and comparison of coefficients proves the injection. Apply [lem-exc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization] to obtain these injections over $Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to each injection and tensor with $R$ over $Q$. The quotient tensor is $R$ modulo the corresponding prefix, as follows directly by sending $r\otimes\bar a$ to $ra$ modulo that prefix, with inverse $\bar r\mapsto r\otimes1$. Thus all the successive multiplications over $R$ are injective. The final quotient is nonzero because all the variables in $L$ belong to the maximal ideal. This is exactly an $R$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

Take $L$ to be all $r$ vanishing coordinates at $x$ and put $J=(z_a:a\in L)\subset R$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$. Step 1 makes $R/J=\mathcal O_{C_L,x}$ regular local. Step 2 and [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] give $\dim(R/J)=\dim R-r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters], $J$ is generated by a prefix $w_1,\ldots,w_c$ of a regular parameter system of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], this prefix has regular quotient of dimension $\dim R-c$, so $c=r$. The classes of this prefix in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ are independent: otherwise a proper subset of the parameter system would span that vector space and, by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] applied to $\mathfrak m$, generate $\mathfrak m$, contradicting the minimal size $\dim R$. Consequently the image of $J$ in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ has dimension $r$. Its $r$ spanning elements $z_a$ are therefore independent. Complete them to a vector-space basis and lift the remaining basis vectors to $\mathfrak m$. Nakayama makes this list generate $\mathfrak m$; its length is $\dim R$, so it is the required regular parameter system [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. For a generic point $\eta$ of any component of a nonempty $C_A$, the regular local ring $\mathcal O_{C_A,\eta}$ is a field. Step 2 and the same dimension formula give $\dim\mathcal O_{V,\eta}=|A|$: each component has codimension $|A|$. The empty subset has zero ideal and gives $V$.

source.place: Tags 00NQ (regular-ring-CM), 00NR (regular-quotient-regular), 00DV (Nakayama local generators); dimension formula for a regular sequence.

proof.text: We record the elementary product calculation that will be used repeatedly. In any of the regular local rings just obtained, let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be distinct members of the supplied parameter system. For each $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes $R/(t_i)$ regular local, and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes it a domain. Thus $(t_i)$ is prime. If $i\ne j$, then $t_j\notin(t_i)$: reducing such an expression modulo $\mathfrak m^2$ would contradict independence of the parameter classes. Inductively, $(t_1)\cap\cdots\cap(t_r)=(t_1\cdots t_r)$: for $f=(t_1\cdots t_{r-1})g\in(t_r)$, primality and the preceding noncontainment force $g\in(t_r)$. The product ideal is consequently radical. Each $t_i$ is a nonzerodivisor in the domain $R$, and so is their product. Coordinates not vanishing at the point are units and do not affect either conclusion. Stalkwise this proves that every product of distinct coordinate factors defines a reduced effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-pc-reduced-scheme], including the empty divisor when all its factors are units. In particular this proves the claims for $B_T$ and $D_S$.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (regular-ring-CM), Tag 00NP (regular-domain); elementary prime-ideal product calculation.

proof.text: Put $I=(z_a:a\in S)$ in $F[z_1,\ldots,z_n]$. The coordinate center $C_S$ is its scheme-theoretic pullback. Since $c$ is flat, the canonical comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. Hence $V^+$ is canonically $V\times_{\mathbf A_F^n}\operatorname{Bl}_I\mathbf A_F^n$. Apply [lem-trf-coordinate-subspace-blowup-charts] with $R=F$, $b=|S|>0$ and $a=n-|S|$, simply reordering variables. It supplies the open cover indexed by $j\in S$ and polynomial chart coordinates $z_j,u_a$ ($a\in S\setminus\{j\}$), $z_a$ ($a\notin S$), with $z_a=z_ju_a$ for $a\in S\setminus\{j\}$. Pull these charts back to $V^+$. The projection of each pulled-back chart to its polynomial model is the base change of $c$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). These are exactly the smooth maps to affine $n$-space asserted in the item.

Apply the coordinate-map argument of steps 1--3, now to each smooth $V_j^+\to\mathbf A_F^n$. It proves all the asserted smoothness, reducedness, regularity, intersection codimensions and parameter extensions on that chart. Put $t=z_j$, $q=\prod_{a\in S\setminus\{j\}}u_a$, $h=\prod_{a\in T\setminus S}z_a$, $s=|S|$. The center ideal pulls back to $(t,tu_a:a\in S\setminus\{j\})=(t)$, so the exceptional inverse-image divisor is $V(t)$, with $t$ a nonzerodivisor by step 4 applied to the chart. Substitution gives the full inverse-image equation $t^s qh$. For every prime ideal, containment of $t^s qh$ is equivalent to containment of $tqh$, so their radicals agree. Step 4 proves $(tqh)$ radical in every chart stalk. Thus the reduced full inverse image has exactly equation $tqh=0$, as claimed [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction].

source.place: Tag 0H1H (remark-relative-blowup), exceptional equation; ILO VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, coordinate substitution.

proof.text: The center is of finite presentation: locally its closed immersion is the quotient by the finite list $(z_a:a∈ S)$. On the $j$-chart the complement of the center is $D(t)$, since its pulled-back ideal is $(t)$. The equation of the pulled-back $D_S$ is $t^s q$, so on $D(t)$ it is $q=0$. By [def-nagata-strict-transform] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], its schematic closure is the kernel of $A\to(A/(q))[1/t]$ on any affine subchart with coordinate ring $A$. This immersion is quasi-compact: its image is closed in the principal open $D(t)$. We show its kernel is exactly $(q)$ by checking stalks. In a chart stalk $R$, discard the unit factors of $q$. If none remain, $q$ is a unit and the claim is immediate. Otherwise each remaining $(u_a)$ is prime and $t\notin(u_a)$ by step 4 (if $t$ is a unit this is automatic). An element $f$ in the kernel satisfies $t^Nf\in(q)$ for some $N\geq0$, by the defining equality criterion in a localization. Primality then gives $f\in(u_a)$ for every remaining factor. Their intersection is $(q)$ by step 4. Conversely every multiple of $q$ maps to zero. Thus the closure, and therefore the strict transform, has equation $q=0$ scheme-theoretically, rather than merely the same support.

source.place: ILO VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p.121, strict-transform coordinate computation; Stacks divisors.tex Tag 080D (definition-strict-transform).

proof.text: If $|S|=1$, the sole affine model of step 5 has no ratio variables and is $\mathbf A_F^n$ with its identity map to the original affine space. Its pullback is therefore $V$, so the blowup is the identity. In step 7 the product $q$ is the empty product $1$, and its zero scheme is empty. When a center or intersection is empty, all preceding pullback and local calculations still hold; there is simply no point at which its codimension must be checked. For $n=0$ the only subset $A$ is empty and there are no nonempty $S$. Every calculation took place on an affine chart or a stalk, so no separatedness, integrality or global quasi-compactness was assumed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q131-3fbb1ea77 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Plain S1 split with no new nodes and the statement unchanged. I read the item's 8 steps and every cited statement, plus Stacks 0H1H (more-morphisms.tex 4940-4972) and ILO VIII Lemma 4.2.9 (p.121); the item states the ILO chart computation. Steps: (1) C_A is a base change of c to A^{n-|A|}, so it is smooth, then regular (056S) and reduced. (2) Flat Q->R carries the variable sequence to an R-regular sequence, using weak-regularity localization and flat tensor exactness. (3) The dimension formula, 00NR and 00NQ give a prefix of length r; the z_a classes are then independent in m/m^2 and Nakayama extends them to a regular system of parameters. Codimension is computed at generic points, where the local ring is a field. (4) The product of distinct parameters is radical and a nonzerodivisor; the induction is written out. (5) Flat base change of the blowup plus the 0H1H charts with R=F; the chart maps are base changes of c, so smooth. (6) The reduced total transform has equation tqh. (7) The strict-transform kernel {f: t^N f in (q)} equals (q), checked on stalks by primality, and the immersion is quasi-compact. (8) |S|=1 gives the identity blowup with q=1, and n=0 is covered. Edge cases tested: S={j}, and S=T={1,2} on A^2. Duplicate search: lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry and lem-trf-etale-coordinate-intersection-geometry are not duplicates. The 4 generic tool_uses are accepted. No SGA citation; no fixes.
